pending_commit.commit_message: lakitu: Build kyber/bfq scheduler as module. This allows COS users to experiment on kyber/bfq scheduler. They will need to first insert the kernel module, then switch each block device to it. Below are the commands to verify this: bfq-m /home/xueweiz # cat /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler [mq-deadline] none bfq-m /home/xueweiz # insmod /lib/modules/4.14.91/kernel/block/bfq.ko bfq-m /home/xueweiz # cat /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler [mq-deadline] bfq none bfq-m /home/xueweiz # echo bfq > /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler bfq-m /home/xueweiz # cat /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler mq-deadline [bfq] none BUG=b:122473241 TEST=tryjob; manually verified mq-deadline is still the default scheduler. RELEASE_NOTE=None Change-Id: I48356c09eaa2f6c6e12755fc896390803bbd6f52 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1399364 Commit-Ready: Xuewei Zhang <xueweiz@google.com> Tested-by: Xuewei Zhang <xueweiz@google.com> Reviewed-by: Xuewei Zhang <xueweiz@google.com>

tast: Use go-cmp to compare structs with time.Time fields. Update several unit tests to use cmp.Equal rather than reflect.DeepEqual when comparing structs that contain time.Time fields. Using reflection to compare time.Time values that have been marshaled to JSON and later unmarshaled apparently fails on systems that are using the UTC time zone, likely due to differing time.Location pointers. See https://golang.org/issue/10089 for more discussion. BUG=none TEST=unit tests now pass on a system that's using UTC CQ-DEPEND=I16a19d71ac0ebb949e00587432117ab2e06990e8 Change-Id: I90853701b2dab87dcef872eb632b80a106b4e782 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1397823 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org>

cryptohome, tpm_manager: separates DA info from tpm status Separates DA info from current tpm status in both tpm_manager and cryptohome. Removes the DA lockout check when checking readiness in attestation. We want to stick the definition of TPM readiness to (enabled && owned). If TPM is locked out, any follow-up steps that require TPM to be ready will fail anyway. Also adds a flag in GetTpmStatusRequest to allow optionally showing/hiding version info in the reply. This is pre-work of refactoring the TPM status maintenance parts in cryptohome. The original flag readiness_info_only in GetTpmStatusRequest is removed because it's no longer needed. BUG=None TEST=unit tests; in the console execute the following 3 commands 1. tpm_manager_client status --include_version_info 2. tpm_manager_client status 3. tpm_manager_client get_da_info and make sure the output of 3 isn't in the outputs of 1 or 2, and the output of 2 doesn't include version info. Change-Id: I6027f1ceb4c25480056459957b901775ad7c6bc5 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1391611 Commit-Ready: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: VSOCK: bind to random port for VMADDR_PORT_ANY The old code always starts from fixed port for VMADDR_PORT_ANY. Sometimes when VMM crashed, there is still orphaned vsock which is waiting for close timer, then it could cause connection time out for new started VM if they are trying to connect to same port with same guest cid since the new packets could hit that orphaned vsock. We could also fix this by doing more in vhost_vsock_reset_orphans, but any way, it should be better to start from a random local port instead of a fixed one. Signed-off-by: Lepton Wu <ytht.net@gmail.com> Reviewed-by: Jorgen Hansen <jhansen@vmware.com> Signed-off-by: David S.
